summary: Petition for termination of Bulk Power Transmission Agreement/Long Term Access Agreement dated 24.12.2010 and termination of Tri-partite Transmission Service Agreement dated 15.12.2011. The present batch of Petition Nos. 127 of 2012, 128/TL/2012, and 156/MP/2012 have been remanded back by the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (hereinafter referred to as “the APTEL”) vide common judgment dated 27.5.2025 passed in Appeal Nos. 128 of 2015; 171 of 2015; 60 of 2017 directing the Commission to allow the adjustment of the acquisition costs paid by Powergrid Corporation of India Limited (hereinafter referred ot as “PGCIL”) by taking a suitable measures under the law, either by recovering the money from REC Transmission Project Limited (hereinafter referred to as “RECPTCL”) in light of the observations made therein or by adjusting the same through other modes. 2. Petition No. 127/2012 was filed by PGCIL seeking adoption of transmission charges under Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as “the Act”) for the Vemagiri Transmission System (hereinafter referred to as “the Project”). Whereas, Petition No. 128/TL/2012 was filed by Vemagiri Transmission System Limited seeking a grant of transmission licence under Section 14 of the Act. During the pendency of the aforesaid Petitions, Petition No. 156/MP/2012 was filed by Spectrum Power Generation Limited (hereinafter referred to as “SPGL”) on 10.7.2012, wherein the Commission was informed about the Ministry of Power’s (hereinafter referred to as “MoP”) letter dated 14.3.2012 regarding non-availability of domestic gas to all gas-based project developers and SPGL also submitted therein that upon becoming aware of the non-availability of gas, it requested PGCIL, vide letter dated 30.3.2012, not to take any further action towards execution of the Project and to return the Bank Guarantee amounting to Rs. 67.50 crore. SPGL also requested RECPTCL [now known as REC Power Development and Consultancy Limited (RECPDCL)], vide allowed the review to the limited extent of deferring the final determination of liability in respect of the remaining 20% until the disposal of the related appeals filed by SPL _“Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, we are of the opinion that no grounds are made out to interfere with impugned judgment/order passed by the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity, New Delhi, on principles of fairness as well as restitution._ _However, question of law, if any, is left open to be considered in an appropriate case. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.”_ 10. Vide Record of Proceedings dated 19.12.2025, the parties were directed to file their written submissions within a week with a copy to the other side. Subject to the above, the matter was reserved for Order. 2.2.2026, reiterating the earlier rounds of litigation and, _inter alia_ , has submitted as (c) The Commission, vide order dated 6.4.2015 (as modified by order dated 20.10.2016), as well as the APTEL, vide Order dated 27.5.2025, have 13. We have considered the submissions made by PGCIL and examined the material made available on record. As noted above, the APTEL has remanded the matter to this Commission vide its judgment dated 27.5.2025 in Appeal Nos. 128 of 2015, 171 of 2015 and 60 of 2017 (affirmed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court vide order provisions of the Act. The APTEL observed that RECTPCL, despite being fully aware of the Force Majeure situation arising from the MoP’s communication dated 14.3.2012 and SPGL’s letters dated 30.3.2012 and 6.4.2012 seeking cancellation/deferment, failed to defer the acquisition process, approach the Ministry of Power or the Empowered Committee on Transmission for reconsideration, or exercise its discretionary power under Clause 2.4(e) of the RfP to extend timelines or keep the bidding in abeyance. The APTEL also criticized RECTPCL for its failure to place relevant documents and communications on record to justify its insistence on proceeding with the acquisition, describing such conduct as undermining its duty to ensure proper coordination and implementation of the transmission system in a fair and transparent manner. The APTEL also rejected the RECPTCL’s submission of jurisdiction over it and held that the actions of RECTPCL fall within the jurisdiction of this Commission. Further, while rejecting the contentions that its role as BPC ceased after the acquisition of the VTSL and that any claim for reimbursement of fees or acquisition price violates the covenants of guidelines, RfP and the Share Purchase Agreement, the APTEL also noted that, on being asked, RECPTCL could not even provide the details of expenditure incurred by them. the extent for which the matter was remanded. The Court below, to which the matter is remanded by the Superior Court, is bound to act within the scope of remand, and it is not open to the Court below to do anything but to carry out the terms of remand in letter and spirit. In the present case, the direction in the APTEL’s judgment being limited to the adjustment of the acquisition costs paid by PGCIL, it is impermissible to consider PGCIL’s claims of expenditure of SPV (VTSL) or the carrying cost. Similarly, PGCIL’s claim for reimbursement of the legal costs/expenditure incurred by it in these proceedings is also beyond the scope of the limited remand directed by the APTEL. 21. With this, the directions issued by the APTEL _vide_ judgment dated 27.5.2025 in Appeal Nos. 128 of 2015; 171 of 2015, and 60 of 2017 stand implemented. 22. Petition Nos. 127/2012, 128/TL/2012, and 156/MP/2012 are disposed of in terms of the above.
